memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord then said to Noah, "Go into the ark, you and your whole family, because I have found you righteous in this generation." - Gen 7:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice the tender word God uses: "Go into the ark" - or as older translations put it, "Come." God does not stand at a distance shouting orders; He invites Noah and his family into the place of safety. And notice this too: God says "I have found you righteous," but the Hebrew idea is really "come before me," God Himself already inside the place of refuge, calling His people to where He is.

This is the heart of God throughout the Bible. Judgement was real and near, but before it fell, God's invitation went out - come in, come to safety, come to Me. He does not merely warn of danger; He opens a door and welcomes His people through it.

The invitation extended to Noah's "whole family." God's saving purpose is generous, reaching to households. What a comfort for those praying for their loved ones - God delights to save families.

This same inviting voice calls today. Jesus stands and says, "Come to me, all you who are weary" (Matt 11:28), and "whoever comes to me I will never drive away" (John 6:37). The God of the flood is the God who invites. Salvation is not us climbing up to God, but God opening the door and calling us in. Have you answered His "come"?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you heard and answered God's invitation to come to Him?
- Are you praying for your whole household to come in too?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You do not just warn me of danger but invite me to safety. I hear Your "come," and I come to You through Jesus. Draw my whole family in too.
